harper: hey all, brand new here. building runtime from source per the README but link step fails with a bunch of undefined references to C++ atomics / GLIBCXX symbols. build is inside the official dev container. any onboarding tips? :wave:

harper: excerpt from bazel link error:

harper: ```
/usr/bin/ld: bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin/runtime/libredwood_runtime.so: undefined reference to `__atomic_fetch_add_8
/usr/bin/ld: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6: undefined reference to `std::__cxx11::basic_string<char, std::char_traits<char>, std::allocator<char> >::__append
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

harper: ldd on the produced .so points at /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6 and readelf -s shows required GLIBCXX_3.4.30 symbols which the image might not provide.

mika: welcome! this usually means the runtime was built with a newer libstdc++ (gcc toolchain) than the one present in the container at runtime. which dev container tag are you using? and what does `gcc -v` show inside it?

harper: dev container is `redwood/dev-container:cuda12.2-base` from quickstart. `gcc -v` shows gcc 12.2.0 on the container, but our bazel toolchain is set to use `//tools:gcc14` in the workspace (default for some branches). seems like a mismatch.

jiang: yep, mixing g++ versions will give you GLIBCXX symbol issues. options: 1) build and run with the same toolchain (use a container image that matches gcc14), 2) statically link libstdc++ for the runtime (not ideal), or 3) ensure LD_LIBRARY_PATH points to the newer libstdc++ shipped into the container. devex usually maintains `redwood/dev-container:gcc14-cuda12.2` for this.

harper: tried mounting a newer libstdc++.so.6 into /usr/lib but the loader complains about versioning and then other native deps fail. not great.

tiago: easiest onboarding fix: switch your local container to the matching image (devex: `redwood/dev-container:gcc14-cuda12.2-dev`) or override the bazel toolchain to use system gcc12 with `--crosstool_top=@local_config_cc//:toolchain` for a local build. if you plan to run on infra nodes that have gcc14, prefer the gcc14 container to avoid surprises.

mika: also check `.bazelrc` in your branch; some teams set `build --action_env=LD_LIBRARY_PATH` which can mask these problems in CI. for local dev we try to replicate CI toolchain exactly. devex-bot: note on toolchains added to onboarding doc a while back.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-540: "onboard: GLIBCXX / libstdc++ link errors in dev container" assigned to infra oncall. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-540 :ticket:

harper: thanks, switching to the gcc14 dev image fixed link errors and the smoke binary runs. i'll open a tiny PR to update our quickstart README to mention the gcc14 image for branches that require it. also adding a short note in my onboarding checklist. really appreciate the help! :thumbsup:

jiang: welcome aboard and great catch. PR review happy to help with README snippet.

harper: will do, filing that PR now :rocket:
